name: get_document
description: Read the open easyCAD document: name, path, revision, unsaved flag, parameters (expression and value), sketches (solve status, DOF, closed regions), features in history order (id, name, type, full definition, regen status and summary), bodies (id, name, bounding box), the undo history and what the app is doing (a dialog or sketch open). `user_changes` lists edits the user made in the app since your last call: read it before every change and build on the user's edits instead of overwriting them. Feature definitions use the same JSON as add_feature / edit_feature. It reads the whole committed document: what the user hides, cuts or rolls back in their window does not change it.

include_definitions.description: Include each feature's full `kind` JSON (default true). Set false for a short overview of long histories.

name: set_param
description: Create or change user parameters (mm and degrees; expressions like "wall*2 + 0.2", "1/8 in", "max(3, w/10)"). Several parameters in one call are one undo step. Waits for regeneration and returns every feature's status, so you see what the change broke. Prefer named parameters over literals in sketches and features: the user can then tweak the design from the Parameters panel.

name.description: Parameter name (letters, digits, _; not a unit or function name).

comment.description: Optional note shown next to the parameter.

params.description: Set several at once instead of name/expr.

delete.description: Parameter names to remove (refused while anything still uses them).

expected_revision.description: Refuse if the document revision moved (the user edited since you looked).

name: add_sketch
description: Add (or replace) a constrained 2D sketch and solve it. Elements: `rect` ({center,width,height} fully constrained, or {min,max} with only H/V constraints), `rounded_rect` ({center,width,height,radius}, fully constrained), `circle` ({center, radius|diameter}, centre fixed), `line` ({from,to}), `arc` ({center,start,end}, counter-clockwise), `point` ({at}). Coordinates are numbers in plane units (mm); sizes (width, height, radius, diameter, constraint values) are expressions such as "width" or "wall*2". Give elements an `id` to reference them in constraints: rect lines `<id>.bottom/.right/.top/.left`, corners `<id>.bl/.br/.tr/.tl`, centre `<id>.center`; rounded_rect lines plus arcs `<id>.arc_br/.arc_tr/.arc_tl/.arc_bl`; any line's ends `<id>.a/.b`; an arc's `<id>.center/.start/.end`; a circle's `<id>.center`; raw indices `#p3` / `#e2`. Constraint types: coincident{a,b}, horizontal{entity}, vertical{entity}, parallel{a,b}, perpendicular{a,b}, tangent{a,b}, equal{a,b}, point_on_line{point,entity}, point_on_circle{point,entity}, midpoint{point,entity}, symmetric{a,b,line}, fix{point,at?}, distance{a,b,value}, distance_x{a,b,value}, distance_y{a,b,value}, point_line_distance{point,entity,value}, length{entity,value}, radius{entity,value}, diameter{entity,value}, angle{a,b,value}. Returns the sketch id, the solve report (status, DOF, residual), the closed regions found and the names you can reference. A sketch that does not converge or conflicts is not added.

plane.description: "XY" (normal +Z), "XZ" (front plane, normal -Y, x along +X), "YZ" (normal +X, x along +Y), or {origin:[x,y,z], x_dir:[..], normal:[..]}.

offset.description: Move the plane along its normal (mm).

replace.description: Replace the sketch with this id (features using it follow).

name: add_feature

name.description: Feature name shown in the history, e.g. "Bin body".

position.description: Insert before this history index instead of at the end.

keep_on_error.description: Keep the feature even if it fails (default false).

name: import_mesh
description: Import a triangle mesh (STL, OBJ, GLB or glTF) from disk as a mesh body: a closed solid made of triangles that can be moved (TransformBody), split (Split, e.g. a flat bottom with keep: Above) and combined with solid bodies (MeshBoolean: Join / Cut / Intersect with clearance, at several positions). It is placed as stored in the file unless you give scale / rotate_deg / translate (applied in that order after the up-axis turn; all editable later with edit_feature on the ImportMesh feature, expressions allowed). The file is read and checked first: open or non-manifold meshes are repaired (welded, reoriented, holes filled) or refused with the count of bad edges. Returns the feature report and bodies; the body id is {"feature": <feature id>, "index": 0}.

path.description: Absolute path to a .stl, .obj, .glb or .gltf file.

name.description: Feature / body name (default: the file name).

up.description: The file's up axis. Default Y for .glb/.gltf (turned so it stands up along +Z), Z otherwise (coordinates used as they are).

scale.description: Uniform scale about the file origin (number or expression, default 1).

rotate_deg.description: XYZ Euler rotation in degrees about the origin (default [0,0,0]).

translate.description: [x, y, z] in mm, numbers or expressions (default [0,0,0]).

reference.description: Reference body: shown, never booleaned or printed (default false).

name: edit_feature
description: Change a feature by id: a new `kind` definition (same JSON as add_feature; get the current one from get_document), a new `name`, or `suppressed`. One undo step. Regenerates and reports. If the edit makes a previously working feature fail it is reverted unless keep_on_error is true.

name: delete_feature
description: Delete a feature by id (one undo step). Features that depended on its bodies will report errors: the reply lists them.

name: regenerate
description: Wait for the model to finish regenerating and return every feature's report: status (ok / warning / error / unresolved reference / suppressed), fillet and chamfer summaries (edges applied, reduced, failed with their largest workable size), sketch solve reports, timing, and the resulting bodies.

name: measure
description: Measure bodies: bounding box, volume, surface area, and optionally the faces and edges, each with what made it ("Body · side", "Shell · floor"), its geometry and a ready-to-use selector for add_feature / edit_feature. Use it to find the faces to shell or the edges to fillet. It reads the whole committed document: what the user hides, cuts or rolls back in their window does not change it. Mesh bodies report `mesh: {triangles, watertight}` and have no faces or edges to select.

body.description: Body name or {feature,index}; omit for all bodies.

limit.description: At most this many faces / edges per body (default 80).

name: get_selection
description: What the user has selected in the viewport right now (bodies, faces, edges), with geometry, what made each face, and selectors you can use directly. Use it when the user says "this face" or "these edges".

name: interference
description: Check solid bodies (or assembly components) for overlaps: each interfering pair with its common volume. Use it to check that a lid, a PCB or a part does not collide with the body. It reads the whole committed document: what the user hides, cuts or rolls back in their window does not change it.

include_reference.description: Include reference bodies such as imported PCBs and library parts (default true).

name: screenshot
description: A PNG of the model, rendered offscreen from your own view. It is separate from the user's window: their camera, hidden bodies, section, display mode, selection or open sketch never change your picture, and your calls never move their view. Your view (camera, hidden bodies, section, display) is kept from call to call; every reply shows it, and view_state resets it. `view` turns your camera to a view-cube direction and keeps it there: "iso", "front" (looking along +Y), "back", "left", "right", "top", "bottom", or combinations such as "top front right" (corners) and "front right" (edges). "current" (the default) is your last view, and "user" copies the user's camera, to see what they are looking at. `views` takes up to 6 directions as one labelled contact sheet (e.g. ["front","top","right","iso"]) without moving your camera: use it to check proportions in one call. `highlight` paints faces, edges, the faces a feature made, or whole bodies orange and fades every other body (this picture only), so you can confirm what a selector picks before you use it in add_feature. `section` cuts the model with a plane (x, y or z, at a coordinate in mm) to show walls, cavities and parts inside, and stays on until `section: null`. A new cut with no view given looks straight at it. `hide`, `show` (or "all") and `isolate` take body names and persist. `xray` (this picture only) draws every body see-through. `display` persists: "shaded", "edges" or "wireframe".

view.description: View direction, "current" (default: your last view) or "user" (the user's camera). Kept for later calls.

views.description: Several directions as one contact sheet (1-6); your camera stays where it was.

fit.description: Zoom to fit the bodies drawn (default true for named views, false for current/user).

features.description: Feature ids: the faces each one made.

body.description: Resolve face/edge selectors on this body only (name or {feature,index}); default every body.

ghost.description: Fade the bodies that are not highlighted (default true when highlighting). This picture only.

xray.description: Draw every body see-through, to show parts inside others. This picture only.

at.description: Plane position in mm along the axis (default the middle of the model).

keep.description: Which side of the plane stays (default below, i.e. smaller coordinates).

hide.description: Body names (or {feature,index}) to leave out of your view from now on.

isolate.description: Show only these bodies in your view from now on (`show: "all"` undoes it).

max_width.description: Width of the returned PNG in pixels (default 1024).

show.description: Body names to bring back into your view, or "all".

reset_view.description: Start from the default view (iso, fitted, everything shown, no section) before applying the rest.

name: view_state
description: Your own view of the model (camera direction, hidden bodies, section, display), which screenshot keeps from call to call. It is separate from the user's window in both directions. `reset: true` goes back to the default: iso, fitted, every body shown, no section.

name: export
description: Export the solid bodies to a file: STL or 3MF (printing; the active process profile's compensations apply) or STEP. The format follows the extension unless given. The path must be absolute and its folder must exist. Mesh bodies go to STL/3MF as their (watertight) triangles; STEP leaves them out.

include_reference.description: Include reference bodies (STEP only; default false).

orient_to_plate.description: Apply each body's build orientation (STL/3MF; default true).

name: open_document
description: Open a .ecad document folder in the app. Refused when the open document has unsaved changes unless discard_unsaved is true (ask the user first).

name: new_document
description: Start a new empty document in the app. Refused when the open document has unsaved changes unless discard_unsaved is true (ask the user first).

name: save_document
description: Save the document: to its current .ecad folder, or to `path` (an absolute path; .ecad is added).

name: undo
description: Undo the last step. By default only your own steps (labelled "Claude: ...") are undone; anything else is refused so you never undo the user's work by accident.

allow_user_steps.description: Also undo a step the user made (only when the user asked).
